title: 2023 capital budget and 10-year forecast review
subtitle: Debt and development charges, reserves, urban forestry, community grants, trails and cycling, council chamber technology, park garbage collection.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee reviewed the 2023 Capital Budget and 10-year forecast, hearing from the Chief Financial Officer and staff on funding sources, debt, development charges and reserve funds, then going through the forecast section by section. Staff said most spending goes to replacing and renewing existing assets, and that some project costs have risen because of inflation and supply chain shortages, so timelines were adjusted to fit available funding.

Staff warned that development charge reserves are projected to turn negative for several years because of large growth-related projects, and that Bill 23 could force the City to defer projects or issue debt. A report on those effects is expected to go to Council in the first half of 2023.

The committee made no final budget changes. It passed one resolution directing staff to report back with more information on seven matters before the final budget day: internal borrowing instead of debt, the Urban Forestry budget, two community grants, Council Home Technology, Grand River Park, shifting cycling money to trail paving, and garbage collection in parks and trails. Any recommendations were to be considered at a Special Council meeting later the same day.

decisions.detail: The committee directed staff to report on borrowing internally from reserves rather than issuing debt, including the existing Capital Funding and Debt policy.
The committee directed staff to report on the impact of reducing the Urban Forestry budget by $100,000 a year ($1M in total).

decisions.item: RISE and Love My Hood grants
decisions.detail: The committee directed staff to report on raising funding for each grant by $25K or $50K, and on how an increase would be funded.
The committee directed staff to report on the Council Home Technology allocation and whether it is adequate for the term of Council.
The committee directed staff to report on the resourcing needs and cost of developing Grand River Park.
The committee directed staff to report on moving $300k a year from cycling infrastructure to paving trails.

decisions.item: Garbage collection in parks and trails
decisions.detail: The committee directed staff to report on options for enhanced garbage collection in parks and trails.

debate: On debt, one councillor asked whether short-term needs could be covered by borrowing from reserves and repaying within the policy's five-year limit. Staff noted that debt for development charge projects would be repaid from those charges, not by taxpayers. The request for an issue paper also asked about the timing of issuing debt, given expected interest rates.

On Bill 23, staff said the full effect is unknown while provincial regulations are pending, and the forecast was not adjusted. A councillor asked if projects should be delayed. Staff said they could not yet say, and that they would bring options such as more debt, deferring projects or other funding sources.

On Urban Forestry, one councillor asked about phasing the funding in later, given financial pressures. Staff said early tree planting is key to reaching the approved canopy targets. Another councillor cautioned that trees help with heat and cooling, so cuts could cost more later.

On Council Chamber audio-visual upgrades, a councillor asked to separate hybrid-meeting costs from basic repairs. Staff said the equipment is at end of life, that piecemeal fixes had already cost money, and that the work is best done as one scope or deferred. The councillor then withdrew the request.
Members discussed the RISE and Love My Hood grants. Some supported more money given demand. Staff preferred building the programs up gradually, with a staff report on longer-term funding to follow.

On trails and cycling, a councillor wanted more paved trails that link to the cycling network. Staff said moving the money would make it harder to meet short-term cycling network targets, and that master plan priorities could be revisited in a progress update.
